appeared before Judge Helmick at the American Consular

During the p.m. of 5-9-40, with the authority of
Mr. Richardson, U.S. Marshal, the undersigned interviewed
Mrs. Jose at Ward Road Gaol, when she was informed that
the stolen property had been recovered and asked if she
wished to make a statement, she replied "I did not do it,
and will not say anything."

On 5-9-40, notification was received from the
American Consulate requesting that Mrs. Hose be taken
there at 10 a.m. on 6-9-40, for questioning by the acting
District Attorney Mr. Richardson and arraignment before
the U.S. Consular Court.

Mr. Richardson, first questioned Mrs. Jose, who
steadfastly denied the theft, however, two charges of
Grand Theft, were filed against her and Major H. D. Rodger,
appointed to defend her. She was then taken before Judge
M.J. Helmick, who heard the charges against her and
arrangements for her defence, after which he arranged
that the case come up for trial at 2 p.m. on 11-9-40.

Mr. Richardson instructed the undersigned to take
complt. and the three witnesses to see him at 10 a.m. on
11-9-40.

1940年9月5日下午，经美国法警Richardson先生授权，具名人在华德路监狱讯问了Jose夫人，告知她被盗财物已被追回，并询问她是否愿意发表声明，她回答说：“我没做，我什么也不说。”

1940年9月5日，收到美国领事馆通知，要求于1940年9月6日上午10时将Hose夫人带至该处，由代理地区检察官Richardson先生进行讯问，并在美国领事法庭提审。

Richardson先生首先讯问了Jose夫人，她坚决否认盗窃，尽管如此，仍对她提出两项重大盗窃罪指控，并指派H. D. Rodger少校为其辩护。随后她被带到M.J. Helmick法官面前，法官听取了对她的指控及辩护安排，之后他安排案件于1940年9月11日下午2时开庭审理。

Richardson先生指示具名人带领原告及三名证人于1940年9月11日上午10时去见他。

Mrs. Conchita Martinez,
Philippines D.S. Crossley
L.160/192, N.
Szechuen Road 4-9-40

On the a.m. of 3-9-40, a police officer accompanied by
Mrs. Resurreccion came to my home No.192, Lane No.180 N.
Szechuen Road, to inquire regarding one Mrs. Jose, a friend
who occasionally visits me and was alleged to have stolen a
box containing money and jewellery, the property of Mrs.
Resurreccion, however, I had not seen Mrs. Jose for three
days and having informed the police officer of this fact,
he and Mrs. Resurreccion went away.

Shortly following their departure, Mrs. Jose, entered
my house via the rear door carrying a small leather box bound
with string and without speaking to me or Mrs. Roma, who
was with me proceeded up the stairway to a loft room situate
between the ground and upstairs front rooms, where she placed
the box and immediately left without giving any explanation
for her action. Both I and Mrs. Roma, suspected the box to
be that stolen from Mrs. Resurreccion and at about 1 p.m.
Mrs. Roma's husband went to Mrs. Resurreccion's home to inform
her of the occurrence and upon failing to find her there, a
friend Mrs. Ines Deramos, was requested to locate and inform
Mrs. Resurreccion. At about 5.30 p.m. Mrs. Resurreccion
accompanied by a police officer arrived at my home and after
checking the contents of the box, took it away.

This is my true statement.

(Signed)
Conseria L. martinez
pages.zh:
Conchita Martinez夫人，
菲律宾 D.S. Crossley
北四川路180弄192号，L.160/192, N.
1940年9月4日

1940年9月3日上午，一名警官陪同Resurreccion女士来到我家，地址为北四川路180弄192号，查询一位名叫Jose的夫人，她是偶尔来访我的朋友，据称她偷窃了一个装有现金和珠宝的箱子，该财物属于Resurreccion夫人，然而，我已经三天没见到Jose夫人了，在将此事实告知警官后，他和Resurreccion女士便离开了。

在他们离开后不久，Jose夫人通过后门进入我家，手里拿着一个用绳子捆扎的小皮箱，没有和我或与我在一起的Roma夫人说话，便走上楼梯，来到位于底层和前楼之间的一间阁楼房间，她把箱子放在那里，随即离开，对其行为未作任何解释。我和Roma夫人都怀疑这个箱子就是从Resurreccion夫人那里偷来的，下午1点左右，Roma夫人的丈夫去Resurreccion夫人家告知此事，因未在那里找到她，便请求一位朋友Ines Deramos夫人寻找并通知Resurreccion夫人。下午5点30分左右，Resurreccion夫人在一名警官的陪同下到达我家，在检查了箱内物品后，将箱子带走。

这是我的真实陈述。

（签名）
Conseria L. martinez

Mrs. Anastacia Roma
Philippines D.S. Crossley
No.180/192 N.
Szechuen Road 4-9-40

During the A.M. of 3-9-40, a foreign police officer
accompanied by Mrs. Resurreccion, came to my home No.192,
Lane No.130 North Szechuen Road, and inquired of me whether
a friend of mine Mrs. Jose had called to see me recently
stating she had stolen a box containing money and jewellery.
I replied that I had not seen Mrs. Jose for three days, where-
upon the police officer and Mrs. Resurreccion, took their
leave.

Some short time following their departure Mrs. Jose
entered the house via the rear door carrying a brown leather
box bound with string which she took upstairs and placed in
a small loft room over the ground floor front. She then left
without attempting to speak to either one of Mrs. Martinez,
with whom I was sitting in the ground floor front room.

We both suspected that the box left by Mrs. Jose must be
that stolen from Mrs. Resurreccion and at about 1 P.M., I
requested my husband to go to Mrs. Resurreccion's home and
inform her of the incident, he, however, later returned and
stated that she was not at home. A friend of mine Mrs. Ines
Daramos, was then approached and asked to locate and inform
Mrs. Resurreccion, with the result that at about 5.30 P.M., the
police officer accompanied by Mrs. Resurreccion arrived at my
home and upon the box being identified as Mrs. Resurreccion's
property and contents checked it was taken away.

(Signed)
Anastacia
Roma

Anastacia Roma夫人
菲律宾 D.S. Crossley
北四川路180/192号
1940年9月4日

1940年9月3日上午，一名外籍警官陪同Resurreccion女士来到我家，地址为北四川路130弄192号，向我询问我的朋友Jose夫人最近是否来看过我，并称她偷窃了一个装有现金和珠宝的箱子。我回答说我已经三天没见到Jose夫人了，于是警官和Resurreccion女士便告辞离去。

在他们离开后不久，Jose夫人通过后门进入屋内，手里拿着一个用绳子捆扎的棕色皮箱，她带上楼，放在底层前厅上方的一间小阁楼房间里。然后她离开，没有试图与坐在底层前厅的Martinez夫人中的任何一位交谈，当时我正与她们在一起。

我们都怀疑Jose夫人留下的箱子一定是从Resurreccion夫人那里偷来的，下午1点左右，我请我丈夫去Resurreccion夫人家告知此事，但他后来回来说她不在家。随后联系了我的朋友Ines Daramos夫人，请她寻找并通知Resurreccion夫人，结果是下午5点30分左右，警官陪同Resurreccion夫人来到我家，在确认该箱子为Resurreccion夫人的财产并检查了内容物后，将其带走。

（签名）
Anastacia
Roma

Mrs. Pacuraviu.
D.S. Crossley
Russia
No.74 Chapoo
Road
4-9-40.

I am the chief tenant of No.74 Chapoo Road, a portion
of the rooms of the premises being sub-let by me to Mrs.
Resurreccion, Mrs. Jose and two other people.
At about 9 p.m. on 2-9-40, whilst I was sat in the
ground floor front room conversing with a male friend, I saw
Mrs. Jose, who was carrying some thing wrapped in a reddish
coloured bed cover pass by my room door, to gain the front
door and leave the premises. Knowing that Mrs. Resurreccion
was absent and that Mrs. Jose had free access to her room, I
felt suspicious and about 15 minutes later when Mrs. Jose
returned carrying the bed cover folded over her arm but minus
whatever had been wrapped in it, I approached her stating "you
tell me what you have stolen and bring it back, then I will
not say anything about it to anyone."
She denied having taken anything stating if I wished
I could call the police.
Next day I saw Mrs. Jose leave my house at about 8.30a.m.
and later I saw and informed Mrs. Resurreccion regarding the
incident of the previous night and advised her to check up
her belongings in order to ascertain whether anything was
missing. Later she informed me that a leather case containing
money and jewellery had been stolen, she then went to the
police station to report the matter.

(Signed)
M. M. Pacurariu
pages.zh:
Pacuraviu夫人。
D.S. Crossley
俄国
乍浦路74号
1940年9月4日。

我是乍浦路74号的主要承租人，我将该处部分房间转租给了Resurreccion夫人、Jose夫人和其他两人。
1940年9月2日晚上9点左右，当我坐在底层前厅与一位男性朋友交谈时，我看见Jose夫人拿着一些用红褐色床罩包裹的东西经过我的房门，走向前门并离开了该处。我知道Resurreccion夫人不在家，而Jose夫人可以自由进入她的房间，我感到可疑，大约15分钟后，当Jose夫人回来时，臂弯里折叠着床罩，但里面包裹的东西不见了，我走近她说：“你告诉我你偷了什么并把它带回来，我就不会向任何人提起这件事。”
她否认拿了任何东西，说如果我愿意可以叫警察。
第二天，我看见Jose夫人在上午8点30分左右离开我家，后来我见到并告知了Resurreccion夫人前一晚的事件，建议她检查自己的物品以确定是否有丢失。后来她告诉我，一个装有现金和珠宝的皮箱被偷了，随后她去警察局报了案。

（签名）
M. M. Pacurariu

pages.en:
At 10.05 a.m. on 3/9/40, Mrs. Salud. I.
Resurreccion, reported to the station, to the effect
that a brown leather attache case containing local
currency, Philippine peso's, jewellery, pawn papers
and personal paper etc, total value $1,311. 00, had
been stolen from a room which she occupies on the
1st floor of House No.74 Chapoo Road and in view of
certain information which she had received from the
chief tenant of the House one Mrs. M. Pacuravlu,
Austrian subject, she suspected one Mrs. Bibiana
Lucia Jose, Philippine, a friend, who also resides
on the premises to be responsible for the crime.
Questioned by the undersigned, complt.
stated that she arrived Shanghai during March 1940,
in company with her husband and seven year old
daughter and took up residence in the French Con-
cession. During June her husband deserted her and
she then resided alone with her daughter until the
early part of July, when in the home of a Philippine
friend, she met Mrs. Bibiana Lucia Jose, who had
also been deserted by her husband and was in a state
of destitution, being entirely dependant on the
charity of various friends she possessed amongst
the Philippine community of Shanghai.
Feeling sorry for Mrs. Jose, she offered
free accommodation and food in her home, this was
readily accepted and shortly afterwards they moved
from the French Concession to their present abode.
However, about two weeks ago, she became acquainted
with an European, whose nationality she does not
pages.zh:
1940年9月3日上午10:05，Salud I. Resurreccion夫人到警局报案，称一个棕色皮革公文包被盗，内含本地货币、菲律宾比索、珠宝、当票及个人文件等，总价值1,311.00美元，该公文包是从她居住的乍浦路74号一楼房间被盗的。鉴于她从该房屋主要承租人M. Pacuravlu夫人（奥地利籍）处获得的一些信息，她怀疑住在同一处的朋友、菲律宾人Bibiana Lucia Jose夫人是罪犯。
经具名人讯问，原告陈述她于1940年3月随丈夫和七岁的女儿抵达上海，并在法租界居住。6月期间，丈夫抛弃了她，此后她与女儿单独居住，直到7月初，在一位菲律宾朋友家中，她遇到了同样被丈夫抛弃且处于贫困状态的Bibiana Lucia Jose夫人，后者完全依赖其在上海菲律宾社区中拥有的各位朋友的慈善救济生活。
出于对Jose夫人的同情，她提供免费食宿，对方欣然接受，不久后她们从法租界搬至目前的住所。然而，大约两周前，她结识了一位欧洲人，其国籍她不

pages.en:
1/3

know, this person coming to live with her. This new
condition made it necessary for Mrs. Jose, to move
from her (complt's) room, this she did and for the sum
of £10.00, per month was permitted by Mrs. Pacuraviu,
to sleep nightly on a mattress in the ground floor central
room of the house, but she still kept her clothing etc.
in complte.'s room and in order that she should be in
no way inconvenienced was allowed to retain possession
of a key to the room.

At 8 p.m. on 2/9/40, complt. in company with her
new paramour and daughter, after securing her room door
proceeded to the Capital Theatre and upon returning
home about 11.15 p.m., retired.

At about 9.30 a.m. on 3/9/40, complte. whilst
on the ground floor portion of the premises, was app-
roached by Mrs. Pacuraviu, who informed her that at
about 9 p.m. on the previous night she had seen Mrs.
Jose, leave the house carrying in her arms some thing
wrapped in a bedcover and about 15 minutes later, she
had returned with the bedcover folded over her arms,
but minus whatever had been wrapped in it. Suspecting
that whatever had been carried out was the property of
complainant, she taxed Mrs. Jose with having committed
theft and advised her to return the property taken and
nothing further would be said regarding the matter.
pages.zh:
1/3

知道，此人随后与她同居。这种新情况使得Jose夫人有必要从她（原告的）房间搬出，她照做了，并经Pacuraviu夫人允许，每月支付10.00英镑，每晚睡在房屋底层中央房间的床垫上，但她仍将衣物等存放在原告的房间里，并且为了不受任何不便，被允许保留该房间的钥匙。

1940年9月2日晚上8点，原告与其新情夫及女儿在锁好房门后，前往大光明大戏院（Capital Theatre），并于当晚11点15分左右回家后休息。

1940年9月3日上午9点30分左右，原告在房屋底层部分区域时，Pacuraviu夫人走近她，告知她前一晚9点左右看见Jose夫人离开房屋，臂弯里抱着用床罩包裹的东西，大约15分钟后，她回来时臂弯里折叠着床罩，但里面包裹的东西不见了。怀疑被带出去的东西是原告的财产，她指责Jose夫人犯有盗窃罪，并建议她归还所拿走的财产，对此事不再多言。

pages.en:
1/4

Mrs. Jose, however, denied the accusation and
went to buy cowri on her settee, where she had slept
the night and left the premises at 8.30 a.m. even date.
Mrs. Pacuraviu, then advised complt. to check up her
belongings in order to ascertain whether any thing was
missing. Complt. immediately returned to her room and
looked first into the wardrobe to find that a brown
leather attache case in which she kept her money and
other valuable possessions, was missing and after a
frantic but futile search of the room for it, came to
the station.

The undersigned accompanied by complt. proceeded
to her home, where Mrs. Pacuraviu, was questioned and
corroborated her story as outlined by complt. adding
that an unknown male friend present had also witnessed
the incident. The fact that if Mrs. Jose was actually
the thief and was able to dispose of the attache case
in a period of 15 minutes, seemed to indicate that she
must have carried it to some place very near complt.'s
home, therefore complt. was requested to bring to mind
any friends that Mrs. Jose may have had residing in the
near vicinity of her home. She stated that she had not
at any time taken a great interest in Mrs. Jose's private
affairs, but knew of two places where Mrs. Jose had
occasionally paid visits and led the undersigned first
pages.zh:
1/4

然而，Jose夫人否认了这一指控，并去购买cowri（原文不清，可能指食物或物品），在她过夜睡的沙发上，并于同日早上8点30分离开了该处。随后，Pacuraviu夫人建议原告检查自己的物品，以确定是否有丢失。原告立即回到房间，首先查看衣柜，发现存放现金和其他贵重物品的棕色皮革公文包不见了，在对房间进行了一番疯狂但徒劳的搜寻后，她来到了警局。

具名人陪同原告前往其住所，在那里讯问了Pacuraviu夫人，她证实了原告所述的故事，并补充说当时在场的一位不知名的男性朋友也目睹了这一事件。如果Jose夫人确实是窃贼，并且能够在15分钟内处理掉公文包，这一事实似乎表明她一定将其带到了离原告家很近的地方，因此要求原告回想一下Jose夫人可能有的居住在附近的朋友。她表示自己从未对Jose夫人的私事表现出极大兴趣，但知道Jose夫人偶尔会去两个地方，并首先引导具名人前往

pages.en:
1/5

to House No.69, Lane No.338 Miller Road, where Philippine people were found residing, but when questioned stated that they had not seen Mrs. Jose for a considerable time, therefore enquiries were continued at House No.192, Lane No.180 North Szechuen Road, where a Mrs. Anastacia Roma, was questioned and stated that she had not seen Mrs. Jose for three days.

By arrangement at 1 p.m. the undersigned again met complt. when effort was made to locate Mrs. Jose at the North of the Soochow Creek, various Philippine's known to be friends of Mrs. Jose were visited without success at Hwa Kee Avenue, Bubbling Well Road and Pacific Gardens, Seymour Road, continuing No.83 Carter Road, was visited where information was received that Mrs. Jose had been there and just left a few seconds prior to the arrival of the undersigned and complt. immediately a search was made along Carter Road and Mrs. Jose, located and taken into custody near Bubbling Well Road. Questioned she strenuously denied having taken complt's property, but admitted as stated by Mrs. Pacuraviu, she had at 9 p.m. on 2/8/40, left No.74 Chacao Road, stating that she did so to purchase food, but stated she had taken no property out with her, however, as it was raining she used her bed cover to place over her hand and shoulders. Following suggestion she wa
pages.zh:
1/5

前往米勒路（Miller Road）338弄69号，发现菲律宾籍人士居住于此，但经询问，他们表示已有很长时间未见过何塞夫人（Mrs. Jose），因此调查工作继续在四川北路（North Szechuen Road）180弄192号进行，在此处对阿纳斯塔西娅·罗马夫人（Mrs. Anastacia Roma）进行了询问，她表示已有三天未见过何塞夫人。

根据安排，下午1时，具名人与投诉人再次会面，试图在苏州河以北地区寻找何塞夫人的下落。在化克路（Hwa Kee Avenue）、静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）以及西摩路（Seymour Road）的太平洋花园（Pacific Gardens），走访了多位已知为何塞夫人朋友的菲律宾人，但未获成功。随后继续前往卡特路（Carter Road）83号，在那里获悉何塞夫人曾到过此处，并在具名人与投诉人到达前几秒钟刚刚离开。随即沿卡特路展开搜寻，在靠近静安寺路处找到何塞夫人并将其拘留。经讯问，她极力否认拿走了投诉人的财物，但承认正如帕库拉维乌夫人（Mrs. Pacuraviu）所述，她于1940年8月2日晚上9时离开了乍浦路（Chacao Road）74号，称这样做是为了购买食物，但声称并未携带任何财物外出；不过，由于当时正在下雨，她用床单盖在手上和肩上。按照建议，她愿

pages.en:
1/6

agreeable to led the undersigned to the shop where she
had purchased the food and led the way to Woochang Road
near North Szechuen Road, where she pointed out three
different Chinese food shops at which she now stated
she examined foods displayed from the outside and
seeing nothing she fancied returned home without
making any purchase.

This lack of witnesses to verify that she did
actually go to Woochang Road, combined with the evi-
dence of Mrs. Paouraviu, and fact that she was the only
person excepting complainant to possess a key to complt.
s room, door of which had not been broken or lock
interferred with to gain entry, indicated that contrary
to her denials she was without doubt responsible for
the theft, therefore together with complt. she was taken
to the American Consulate, where the U.S. Marshall for
China Mr. Charles Richardson, was acquainted with the
ascertained facts of the case against Mrs. Jose and
stated that although the evidence obtained was not
sufficient in his opinion to gain a conviction, he
would order the detention of Mrs. Jose for 48 hours,
pending the police endeavouring to trace the stolen
property or gain other substantial evidence.

He then issued the following document:-
pages.zh:
1/6

意带领具名人前往她购买食物的店铺，并引路至靠近四川北路的武昌路（Woochang Road），在那里她指出了三家不同的中式食品店，并称她现在表示当时只是从外面查看了陈列的食品，因没有看到心仪之物，便未作任何购买而返回家中。

缺乏证人证实她确实去过武昌路，加之帕乌拉维乌夫人（Mrs. Paouraviu）的证词，以及除投诉人外只有她拥有投诉人房间钥匙这一事实——该房间的门未被破坏，锁也未被撬动以进入室内——表明尽管她予以否认，但她无疑对此次盗窃负责。因此，她与投诉人一同被带往美国领事馆，驻华美国法警查尔斯·理查森先生（Mr. Charles Richardson）了解了针对何塞夫人的案件既定事实，并表示虽然在他看来所获证据不足以定罪，但他将命令拘留何塞夫人48小时，以待警方努力追踪被盗财物或获取其他实质性证据。

随后他签发了以下文件：-

pages.en:
1/7.

Commissioner, Shanghai Municipal Police 185
Foochow Road, Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

You will please detain Sribiana L. Jose, citizen
of the Philippine Commonwealth, in Ward Road Jail on
suspicion of grand theft pending further instructions
from this office. Yours truly, Charles Richardson Jr.

Mrs. Jose was then escorted to Ward Road Gaol,
where she was searched, but none of the missing property
found on her person.

Having left the gaol the undersigned returned
to No. 74 Chapoo Road, to further interrogate the inmates
and upon arrival found one Mrs. Ines Daramos, Philippine,
who had called to inform complt. that the missing box
was at House No. 192, Lane No. 180 North Szechuen Road,
the home of Mrs. Roma, who as explained previously had
been interrogated shortly following complt. complaining
to the Police.

This address was visited and the attache case,
both locks broken and tied with string was found in an
unoccupied loft room situate between ground and upstairs
front rooms. The contents were checked by complt. who
upon having completed her examination stated that only
$115.00 local currency was missing.
pages.zh:
1/7.

上海公共租界工部局警务处总监
上海福州路185号。

尊敬的先生：

请因涉嫌重大盗窃罪，将菲律宾自治领公民斯里比亚纳·L·何塞（Sribiana L. Jose）拘押于华德路监狱，等候本办公室的进一步指示。此致，小查尔斯·理查森（Charles Richardson Jr.）

何塞夫人随后被护送至华德路监狱（Ward Road Gaol），对其进行了搜身，但在其身上未发现任何遗失财物。

离开监狱后，具名人返回乍浦路（Chapoo Road）74号，以便进一步讯问住户，到达时发现一位名叫伊内斯·达拉莫斯（Ines Daramos）的菲律宾籍女士，她前来通知投诉人，那只遗失的手提箱位于四川北路180弄192号，即罗马夫人（Mrs. Roma）的住所。如前所述，罗马夫人在投诉人向警方报案后不久曾接受过讯问。

警方走访了该地址，在一个位于底层和前楼之间的空置阁楼房间里，发现了那只手提箱，其两把锁均已损坏，并用绳子捆绑。投诉人对箱内物品进行了核对，检查完毕后表示，仅缺失本地货币115.00元。

pages.en:
1/8

Mrs. Roma, was questioned as to who had placed
the attache case on her premises, and stated that at 10 a.m.
or 10.30 p.m. Mrs. Jose had visited the house and placed
it there, this statement was corroborated by another
Philippino inmate one Mrs. Conchita Martinez, who also
stated she had witnessed the incident.

It may, however, be pointed out that the under-
signed and complt. visited the house at 12.45 a.m. at
which time Mrs. Roma, definately stated that she had
not seen Mrs. Jose for three days and upon being re-
minded of this became quite flustered and averred that
Mrs. Jose had called following the police visit and
that she knowing of the theft had become alarmed and
did not dare notify the station or complt. for some
hours.

This statement on the part of Mrs. Jose did not
sound very truthful and taking into consideration that
the distance between complt's home and Mrs. Roma's home
is only a few hundred yards, it is suspected that Mrs.
Jose, actually took the attache case there between
9 a.m. and 9.15 p.m. on 3/9/40 and that it was actually
there during the time of police enquiries in the morning
Furthermore it is highly probable that Mrs. Roma or
some other inmate upon learning through complt. that
it was stolen and nature of contents, remained silent
pages.zh:
1/8

就谁将手提箱放置在其住处一事对罗马夫人进行了讯问，她表示上午10时或晚上10时30分，何塞夫人曾到访该房屋并将箱子放在那里。这一说法得到了另一位菲律宾籍住户孔奇塔·马丁内斯夫人（Mrs. Conchita Martinez）的佐证，后者也表示目睹了这一情况。

然而，必须指出的是，具名人和投诉人曾在凌晨12时45分访问过该房屋，当时罗马夫人明确声明她已有三天未见过何塞夫人；当被提醒此事时，她变得十分慌乱，并坚称何塞夫人是在警方走访之后才来的，并称她因知晓盗窃案而感到恐慌，因此在数小时内不敢通知警局或投诉人。

何塞夫人的这一说法听起来不太真实，考虑到投诉人住所与罗马夫人住所之间仅有几百码的距离，怀疑何塞夫人实际上是在1940年9月3日上午9时至9时15分之间将手提箱带到那里的，并且在上午警方调查期间，箱子确实就在那里。此外，极有可能是罗马夫人或其他住户在通过投诉人得知箱子被盗及内装物品性质后，保持沉默

pages.en:
1/9

in order to break it open following the departure of
the police and extract the missing money. He reported
presence of the case being made later with the hope
that full responsibility for the money being missing
would fall upon Mrs. Jose.

However, whether or not this suspicion is correct
will undoubtedly be known on 4/9/40, when Mrs. Jose
will be informed of developments and further questioned.

Mrs. Peterson, assistant U.S. Marshall was informed
of the recovery and evidence which establishes Mrs.
Jose to be the thief and instructed that on the a.m. of
4/9/40, complaint be taken to the Consulate to swear out
a complaint against Mrs. Jose.

San. Date 1/oo

pages.zh:

以便在警方离开后撬开箱子，取出缺失的钱款。随后报告箱子的下落，是希望让何塞夫人承担钱款缺失的全部责任。

然而，无论这一怀疑是否正确，在1940年9月4日当何塞夫人被告知事态进展并接受进一步讯问时，无疑将会水落石出。

助理美国法警彼得森夫人（Mrs. Peterson）已获悉财物追回情况以及确立何塞夫人为窃贼的证据，并受命于1940年9月4日上午前往领事馆，对何塞夫人提出正式控告。
